A

Answer

Explicit-memory coverage includes a historical complete 45-question NR/SR × four-memory grid, plus a smaller retained seven-cell run. Earlier 0.5B LoRA and HybridMem pilots also ran. The historical runs survive as summarized results, not raw outputs or adapters in this checkout; none is a paper-scale 7B reproduction.

  1. Retained now: BM25/e5 retrieval, numeric-overlap analysis, and seven QA configurations on nine paired questions.123
  2. Historical only: all eight explicit NR/SR cells on 45 questions; 0.5B AskSFT variants, single-hop probes, SFT+RAG and five-cluster HybridMem.4
  3. Realistic next target: retrieval sweeps and a retained, same-model QA grid if Colab GPU fits. The 45-question Farm run already happened; do not present E3 as its first execution.
  4. Stretch target: recover or rebuild the 0.5B pilots with raw evidence, then expand only if Colab resources permit.

How to read: “retained” means raw local output exists here; “historical” means the run and summary exist in the scout report, but raw outputs or adapters were discarded. “Missing” means a specific paper condition has no matching run.

The historical Farm grid covered Ignoramus, Oracle, SparseRAG and DenseRAG under both NR and SR (45 shared questions). The retained nine-question run covers all NR cells and three SR cells; SR DenseRAG is missing only from that retained run. A 0.5B AskSFT/HybridMem pilot separately used 300 facts and 25 multi-hop questions.42

Core route: E1/E2 → E3 → one explanatory study from E4/E5 or N1/N2. Stop there if that answers your presentation question.

Optional routes: N3 adds MR/DR; N4/N5 require training validation. The arrows show dependencies, not promises that Colab can finish everything.

4

4. What does “only Colab” change in the plan?

  1. Inspect the actual runtime

    Record GPU, VRAM, precision support and persistent storage. No GPU model or session duration is assumed.

  2. Keep a CPU-safe route

    BM25, saved-output scoring, overlap analysis and plotting still support a useful presentation.

  3. Test real-context inference

    Use nine questions and full top-20 contexts. Measure memory, time, truncation and failures before expanding.

  4. Gate every training plan

    Train one step, save, reload and infer before any epoch or cluster sweep.

Conditional, not guaranteed: 4-bit 7B inference may be feasible on a suitable GPU. Context length and generation cache still consume memory; a loaded model is not proof of a runnable experiment.

A smaller model or smaller memory corpus changes the scientific condition. Label that as a scaled study, not a paper-equivalent reproduction.5

No notebooks were supplied in this checkout. The plan does not claim to know what is already executed inside your personal Colab notebooks.

5

5. Pick a presentation scope before spending compute

StoryEvidence neededWhen to choose it
A. Why retrieval strugglesCurrent probes, QA pilot and clearly labeled overlap diagnosticAvailable nowYou need a defensible talk now
B. Can I reproduce explicit-memory trends?A plus E1/E2 and completed local E3; preferably N1 or N2RecommendedBest next target for notebook resources
C. Does learned memory help retrieval?B plus matched N4/N5 controls and saved adaptersStretchOnly after training/reload works

A does not require pretending the whole paper is reproduced. Explain the entire paper in the literature portion, then narrow your experimental claim to the part you tested.

B remains useful if the trend disagrees. A controlled disagreement is a result; inspect sample size, prompts, model and retrieval before explaining it away.

C must show matched controls. A trained adapter without a base-model and RAG comparison does not test the hybrid claim.

7. What decision should I make today?

Choose Story B as the target and keep Story A as the fallback. Run E1/E2 first. Attempt E3 only after the real-context smoke run succeeds. Add one explanatory experiment rather than an unfinished full grid.
